identity.title: A Concentration of Centimeter-sized Grains in the Ophiuchus IRS 48 Dust Trap

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present Very Large Array (VLA) Ka band (34 GHz or 0.9 cm) and ALMA Cycle 2 Band 9 (680 GHz or 0.45 mm) observations at a 0\ensuremath{''}2 resolution of the Oph IRS 48 disk

evidence.quote: The stellar position was set to 16$^h$27$^m$37$^s$.185 -24$^{\circ}$30’35$\ensuremath{''}$39, taken from a Keplerian model fit to the CO isotopologue data

question.value: Are centimeter-sized grains more azimuthally concentrated than millimeter-sized grains in the Oph IRS 48 dust trap, as predicted by dust trapping?

evidence.quote: The distributions of dust emission at 450 $\mu$m and 0.9 cm are compared and we aim to provide confirmation of the dust trap scenario in a transitional disk.
with Band 9 (cite: BaryshevBand9) as part of program 2013.1.00100.S

evidence.quote: three windows have a bandwidth of 937.5 MHz, centered on 661, 659 and 675 GHz, the fourth spectral window was centered on 672 GHz with a bandwidth of 1875 MHz.
The total continuum bandwidth was $\sim$4.7 GHz.

validation.value: Simulated VLA observation of ALMA image; compared flux with earlier DnC data

method.value: Fourth-power Gaussian model fit in uv-plane at both frequencies

evidence.quote: The fitting is performed in the $uv$-plane, with the model visibilities sampled onto the observed spatial frequencies.
we use $\chi^2$ minimization over a grid of $\phi_c,\phi_w,r_c$ and $r_w$ with steps of 1$^{\circ}$ and 1 AU

fitting.value: chi^2 grid minimization; errors from rescaling reduced chi^2 to 1

evidence.quote: The errors are estimated by rescaling the reduced $\chi^2$ to 1.
as still more than 85% of the structure is recovered by the Gaussian intensity equation

method.value: Planck equation with isothermal beam-filling emission at 60 K

evidence.quote: we assume that the peak millimeter emission originates from an isothermal area $\Omega_{\rm beam}$ (sr) of the beam size with $T_{\rm dust}$=60 K.
with $T_{\rm dust}$=60 K

method.value: Spectral index from beam-matched ALMA and VLA images and integrated fluxes; beta from tau at both frequencies

evidence.quote: $\beta$ can be calculated as a function of position by calculating $\tau_{\nu}$ at both frequencies at different positions, assuming $T_{\rm dust}$=60 K

assumptions.value: T_dust 60 K uniform; 200 K and 24 K tested

evidence.quote: for $T_{\rm dust}$=200 K in the center, $\beta=0.6\pm0.1$

results_numeric.quantity: Stellar point source flux at 34 GHz

We find $\beta\sim0.7\pm0.1$ in the center and $\beta\sim1.3\pm0.3$ in the outer parts

findings_qualitative.value: 34 GHz emission is more azimuthally concentrated than 680 GHz and not a filtering effect; 34 GHz also shows a point source at the star, likely ionized gas.

evidence.quote: The 34 GHz continuum emission peaks at the same location, but is much more azimuthally concentrated.

claims.hypothesis: Larger grains are more azimuthally concentrated than smaller ones in the IRS 48 trap
claims.experiment: Fit intensity model to ALMA 680 GHz and VLA 34 GHz images
claims.finding: Supports dust trapping of cm-sized grains, subject to optical depth and temperature assumptions

evidence.quote: marginally consistent with the particle trapping mechanism under the above assumptions

claims.hypothesis: Spectral index varies across the trap
claims.result: alpha 2.6 in center to 3.3 in wings
claims.finding: Consistent with more large particles in center

evidence.quote: The azimuthal trend in $\beta$ is thus consistent with increased dust growth

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Spatial filtering and sensitivity effects ruled out; low temperature hiding narrow mm concentration considered unlikely.

evidence.quote: Spatial filtering can be ruled out as an explanation for the different azimuthal extents

limitations_admitted.value: Optical depth at 680 GHz cannot be measured independently of temperature.

evidence.quote: The optical depth $\tau_{680GHz}$ cannot be measured independently from the temperature with the available data.

referee_caveats_inferred: Beam mismatch between VLA and ALMA
